title: 5. Authorization for Special Issuance and AME Assisted Special Issuance (AASI)

blocks.text: A. Authorization for Special Issuance of a Medical Certificate (Authorization).
blocks.html: A. Authorization for Special Issuance of a Medical Certificate (Authorization).

blocks.text: At the discretion of the Federal Air Surgeon, an Authorization for Special Issuance of a Medical Certificate (Authorization), valid for a specified period, may be granted to a person who does not meet the established medical standards if the person shows to the satisfaction of the Federal Air Surgeon that the duties authorized by the class of medical certificate applied for can be performed without endangering public safety during the period in which the Authorization would be in force. The Federal Air Surgeon may authorize a special medical flight test, practical test, or medical evaluation for this purpose. A medical certificate of the appropriate class may be issued to a person who fails to meet one or more of the established medical standards if that person possesses a valid agency issued Authorization and is otherwise eligible. blocks.text: In granting an Authorization, the Federal Air Surgeon may consider the person's operational experience and any medical facts that may affect the ability of the person to perform airman duties including:
blocks.html: In granting an Authorization, the Federal Air Surgeon may consider the person's operational experience and any medical facts that may affect the ability of the person to perform airman duties including:

blocks.text: - The factors leading to and surrounding the episode;
blocks.html: • The factors leading to and surrounding the episode;

blocks.text: - The combined effect on the person of failing to meet one or more than one requirement of part 67; and
blocks.html: • The combined effect on the person of failing to meet one or more than one requirement of part 67; and

blocks.text: - The prognosis derived from professional consideration of all available information regarding the person.
blocks.html: • The prognosis derived from professional consideration of all available information regarding the person.

blocks.text: In granting an Authorization, the Federal Air Surgeon specifies the class of medical certificate authorized to be issued and may do any or all of the following:
blocks.html: In granting an Authorization, the Federal Air Surgeon specifies the class of medical certificate authorized to be issued and may do any or all of the following:

blocks.text: - Limit the duration of an Authorization;
blocks.html: • Limit the duration of an Authorization;

blocks.text: - Condition the granting of a new Authorization on the results of subsequent medical tests, examinations, or evaluations;
blocks.html: • Condition the granting of a new Authorization on the results of subsequent medical tests, examinations, or evaluations;

blocks.text: - State on the Authorization, and any medical certificate based upon it, any operational limitation needed for safety; or
blocks.html: • State on the Authorization, and any medical certificate based upon it, any operational limitation needed for safety; or

blocks.text: - Condition the continued effect of an Authorization, and any second- or third-class medical certificate based upon it, on compliance with a statement of functional limitations issued to the person in coordination with the Director of Flight Standards or the Director's designee.
blocks.html: • Condition the continued effect of an Authorization, and any second- or third-class medical certificate based upon it, on compliance with a statement of functional limitations issued to the person in coordination with the Director of Flight Standards or the Director's designee.

blocks.text: - In determining whether an Authorization should be granted to an applicant for a third-class medical certificate, the Federal Air Surgeon considers the freedom of an airman, exercising the privileges of a private pilot certificate, to accept reasonable risks to his or her person and property that are not acceptable in the exercise of commercial or airline transport pilot privileges, and, at the same time, considers the need to protect the safety of persons and property in other aircraft and on the ground
blocks.html: • In determining whether an Authorization should be granted to an applicant for a third-class medical certificate, the Federal Air Surgeon considers the freedom of an airman, exercising the privileges of a private pilot certificate, to accept reasonable risks to his or her person and property that are not acceptable in the exercise of commercial or airline transport pilot privileges, and, at the same time, considers the need to protect the safety of persons and property in other aircraft and on the ground

blocks.text: An Authorization granted to a person who does not meet the applicable medical standards of part 67 may be withdrawn, at the discretion of the Federal Air Surgeon, at any time if:
blocks.html: An Authorization granted to a person who does not meet the applicable medical standards of part 67 may be withdrawn, at the discretion of the Federal Air Surgeon, at any time if:

blocks.text: - There is an adverse change in the holder's medical condition;
blocks.html: • There is an adverse change in the holder's medical condition;

blocks.text: - The holder fails to comply with a statement of functional limitations or operational limitations issued as a condition of certification under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401);
blocks.html: • The holder fails to comply with a statement of functional limitations or operational limitations issued as a condition of certification under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401);

blocks.text: - Public safety would be endangered by the holder's exercise of airman privileges;
blocks.html: • Public safety would be endangered by the holder's exercise of airman privileges;

blocks.text: - The holder fails to provide medical information reasonably needed by the Federal Air Surgeon for certification under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401); or
blocks.html: • The holder fails to provide medical information reasonably needed by the Federal Air Surgeon for certification under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401); or

blocks.text: - The holder makes or causes to be made a statement or entry that is the basis for withdrawal of an Authorization under the falsification section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.403).
blocks.html: • The holder makes or causes to be made a statement or entry that is the basis for withdrawal of an Authorization under the falsification section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.403).

blocks.text: A person who has been granted an Authorization under the special issuance section of part 67 ( 14 CFR 67.401 ), based on a special medical flight or practical test, need not take the test again during later medical examinations unless the Federal Air Surgeon determines or has reason to believe that the physical deficiency has or may have degraded to a degree to require another special medical flight test or practical test.
blocks.html: A person who has been granted an Authorization under the special issuance section of part 67 ( 14 CFR 67.401 ), based on a special medical flight or practical test, need not take the test again during later medical examinations unless the Federal Air Surgeon determines or has reason to believe that the physical deficiency has or may have degraded to a degree to require another special medical flight test or practical test.

blocks.text: The authority of the Federal Air Surgeon under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401) is also exercised by the Manager, AMCD, and each RFS.
blocks.html: The authority of the Federal Air Surgeon under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401) is also exercised by the Manager, AMCD, and each RFS.

blocks.text: If an Authorization is withdrawn at any time, the following procedures apply:
blocks.html: If an Authorization is withdrawn at any time, the following procedures apply:

blocks.text: - The holder of the Authorization will be served a letter of withdrawal, stating the reason for the action;
blocks.html: • The holder of the Authorization will be served a letter of withdrawal, stating the reason for the action;

blocks.text: - By not later than 60 days after the service of the letter of withdrawal, the holder of the Authorization may request, in writing, that the Federal Air Surgeon provide for review of the decision to withdraw. The request for review may be accompanied by supporting medical evidence;
blocks.html: • By not later than 60 days after the service of the letter of withdrawal, the holder of the Authorization may request, in writing, that the Federal Air Surgeon provide for review of the decision to withdraw. The request for review may be accompanied by supporting medical evidence;

blocks.text: - Within 60 days of receipt of a request for review, a written final decision either affirming or reversing the decision to withdraw will be issued; and
blocks.html: • Within 60 days of receipt of a request for review, a written final decision either affirming or reversing the decision to withdraw will be issued; and

blocks.text: - A medical certificate rendered invalid pursuant to a withdrawal, in accordance with the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401) shall be surrendered to the Administrator upon request.
blocks.html: • A medical certificate rendered invalid pursuant to a withdrawal, in accordance with the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401) shall be surrendered to the Administrator upon request.

blocks.text: B. AME Assisted Special Issuance (AASI)
blocks.html: B. AME Assisted Special Issuance (AASI)

blocks.text: AME Assisted Special Issuance (AASI) is a process that provides AMEs the ability to re-issue an airman medical certificate under the provisions of an Authorization to an applicant who has a medical condition that is disqualifying under 14 CFR part 67.
blocks.html: AME Assisted Special Issuance (AASI) is a process that provides AMEs the ability to re-issue an airman medical certificate under the provisions of an Authorization to an applicant who has a medical condition that is disqualifying under 14 CFR part 67.

blocks.text: An FAA physician provides the initial certification decision and grants the Authorization in accordance with 14 CFR § 67.401. The Authorization letter is accompanied by

AMEs may re-issue an airman medical certificate under the provisions of an Authorization, if the applicant provides the requisite medical information required for determination. AMEs may not issue initial Authorizations. An AME’s decision or determination is subject to review by the FAA.

blocks.text: Continue Authorization Letter
blocks.html: Continue Authorization Letter

blocks.text: As of May 2023:
blocks.html: As of May 2023:

blocks.text: - If the AME issued an AASI correctly, AAM will no longer send a “continue authorization” letter, in accordance with the last paragraph of the authorization letter:
blocks.html: • If the AME issued an AASI correctly, AAM will no longer send a “continue authorization” letter, in accordance with the last paragraph of the authorization letter:

blocks.text: “Please be advised that as long as reports are submitted as outlined in your Authorization letter, certificates are issued correctly, and there have been no changes in your medical condition(s), no further correspondence will be sent from our office.”
blocks.html: “Please be advised that as long as reports are submitted as outlined in your Authorization letter, certificates are issued correctly, and there have been no changes in your medical condition(s), no further correspondence will be sent from our office.”

blocks.text: - AAM will continue to review AASI documents after an AME issues.
blocks.html: • AAM will continue to review AASI documents after an AME issues.

blocks.text: An individual may receive a Continue Authorization Letter when:
blocks.html: An individual may receive a Continue Authorization Letter when:

blocks.text: - A third-class interim medical certificate is being issued; OR
blocks.html: • A third-class interim medical certificate is being issued; OR

blocks.text: - If the AME made an error on the medical certificate and AAM needs to send a corrected certificate (e.g., forgot to put time limitation); OR
blocks.html: • If the AME made an error on the medical certificate and AAM needs to send a corrected certificate (e.g., forgot to put time limitation); OR

blocks.text: - There was an interim condition where review was required, but no changes to the AASI are needed.
blocks.html: • There was an interim condition where review was required, but no changes to the AASI are needed.
